title: Earthquake Preparation
content: Before an earthquake, families should prepare an emergency plan, identify safe places inside their homes, secure heavy furniture to walls, keep emergency supplies ready, and practice earthquake drills. Important emergency supplies include drinking water, non-perishable food, first aid supplies, flashlight, batteries, portable radio, medicines, important documents, power bank, whistle, blanket, and cash. Pets should be included in emergency preparedness plans. Owners should keep pet food, water, medications, identification tags, and carriers ready for evacuation. Children should be taught earthquake safety in schools through regular drills. They should practice Drop, Cover, and Hold On, follow teachers' instructions, avoid running during shaking, and assemble at designated safe areas after evacuation. Older adults should keep essential medicines nearby, maintain emergency contact information, and seek assistance before entering damaged buildings after an earthquake.
